newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: LANGEBERG BULLISH ON EXPORT PROSPECTS.
newsitem.headline: LANGEBERG BULLISH ON EXPORT PROSPECTS.

text.p: Despite a late start to the season, South African fruit canner Langeberg Holdings Ltd is upbeat about export prospects.

Chief executive Andries van Rensburg told Reuters on Monday that instead of the apricot season ending by mid-December the company was still taking up fruit after delays due to cold weather. Staff have had to work through the Christmas holidays to process the crop.
"The apricot crop is slightly down on last year but the quality is better," he said.
"We took in 24,000 tonnes of apricots last year and it will be about 22,000 to 23,000 this year."
In total the country's Western Cape province apricot crop will be between 50,000 and 52,000 tonnes, he said.
"We are expecting the first peaches just after the New Year. Last year it was about 110,000 tons and this year we expect it to be the same or slightly up on last year."
He said the outlook was "quite positive" for the export season.

International prices for canned apricot halves had firmed although apricot pulp prices were "a bit under pressure" after higher prices had forced some juice manufacturers in Europe to switch to peaches.
"But we do not pack a lot of concentrate," van Rensburg said.
Peach prices were also under pressure because of overproduction by main rival Greece.
"Prices are down by between 7.5 and 10 percent," van Rensburg said.
South African exporters would benefit from the weaker rand but European Union import tariffs would still leave them at a 50 percent cost disadvantage.
There was some uncertainty about the future of South African export incentives such as the general export incentive scheme (GEIS), which was being phased out.

Van Rensburg said Langeberg's marketing drive in the EU would be aided by its strategic alliance with U.S.-based fruit processor and marketer Dole and the investment of about 20 million rand in new plant.
Langeberg's biggest export market remains the EU, but Japan takes 25 percent of its products, which are sold under the Gold Reef brand name.
Van Rensburg said exports to the rest of Africa were also growing, especially for tomato-based products.
